title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (6.0%)
drivers.evidence: Historical promotions show price reductions drive demand; price increases typically reduce it. No past data on 6% increase, but similar increases (10%, 25%) show demand drops. Noise-adjusted promotion lift is x1.45, suggesting a 15% drop is plausible for a price rise.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.3. A 6.0% price increase to $4.08 is a known demand-lowering factor. Past promotions at similar discounts (10%, 25%) show median lifts of x1.75 and x2.18, but noise-adjusted estimates are lower (x1.45). The price increase is not a promotion, so it likely reduces demand. The week after a promotion (2025-10-20) showed x1.08 vs baseline, indicating no significant post-promotion dip. The heatwave (38°C) may increase demand for candy, but no evidence supports this. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but price increase is a clear driver. Adjust downward with medium confidence due to limited past price increase data.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
